newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian senator defends embattled Colston.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian senator defends embattled Colston.

text.p: Australian independent senator Brian Harradine on Thursday defended embattled fellow independent senator Mal Colston, who has been dogged this week by numerous allegations of misusing parliamentary privileges.

Harradine, who shares the balance of power with Colston in the non-government dominated upper house of parliament, said the Queensland senator worked harder than most and should be allowed to remain as deputy president of the senate.
The Labor opposition, of which Colston was a member before his resignation in August last year, has called for Colston to step aside because of the allegations.
"Everybody will say that he's a good deputy president and a good chair of committees," Harradine told Australian Broadcasting Corp radio.
"I don't think there's any doubt about that and I think it's on those grounds that he should be judged."

Colston is currently facing an Australian Federal Police investigation into allegations that he misused an expense allowance and an internal government investigation into whether he rorted a free government car entitlement.
Newspapers also reported on Thursday that Colston had pressured the Australian National University, of which he is a council member, to remark his son's exam papers.

But Harradine accused the Labor Party of gunning for Colston as revenge for his defection from the party last year, which greatly improved the Liberal-National coalition government's success rate in passing legislation through the Senate.
"Would the Labor Party be doing this if Senator Colston was still a member of the Labor Party? I'm sure there's a lot of politics in it and I think it's grubby," Harradine said.
Asked if he thought Colston would survive as the Senate's deputy president, Harradine said: "He's been around for a few years now, hasn't he?"
